title: Organizing and Debugging the Cascade knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Organizing and Debugging the Cascade”?
options: Tracing a property from declaration to computed value
questions.answer_key: Tracing a property from declaration to computed value
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “Tracing a property from declaration to computed value” under “Organizing and Debugging the Cascade”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with organizing and debugging the cascade?
options: Inspect the actual winning declaration and solve the cause before adding a new override or !important.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the actual winning declaration and solve the cause before adding a new override or !important.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Inspect the actual winning declaration and solve the cause before adding a new override or !important. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “Organizing and Debugging the Cascade” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
